title: Remove stale Tailscale devices before bringing the lab back
description:
The destroy on 2026-09-23 left the Tailscale proxy devices behind: grafana, prometheus, alertmanager, loki, demoapp, hello-java, and the operator's own node. They are gone as machines but still hold those hostnames in the tailnet.

When the new cluster starts, the operator registers fresh proxies and Tailscale appends a numeric suffix to any name already taken - grafana-1, loki-1 and so on. That breaks every URL in the scenario READMEs and the LOKI_ADDR in the Python client.

Do this BEFORE the apply if possible, so the new proxies claim the clean names on first registration.

Remove the stale devices at https://login.tailscale.com/admin/machines - they are the ones tagged tagged-devices with no recent activity.
acceptance_criteria: tailscale status shows grafana, prometheus, alertmanager, loki, demoapp and hello-java with no numeric suffix, and curl http://grafana/ answers.
close_reason: Verified 2026-09-28: tailscale status shows grafana, prometheus, alertmanager, loki, demoapp, hello-java with no suffix; curl http://grafana/ returns 200

title: Bring the lab back up: terraform apply, restores from snapshot 435320677
description:
Single command, because var.image is pinned to snapshot 435320677:

  gh workflow run terraform.yml -f action=apply

This recreates the server, firewall, SSH key and the four Cloudflare DNS records. The disk comes back as it was at 2026-09-23 15:41 UTC: scenarios 01 and 02 deployed, hello-java running in apps.

Expect a NEW IPv4 and IPv6. The DNS records follow automatically since Terraform manages them, but SSH will complain about a changed host key - clear the old entry with ssh-keygen -R.

The minikube systemd unit starts the cluster on boot, so give it a few minutes before kubectl works.
acceptance_criteria: kubectl get nodes shows obs-lab Ready, and the scenario 01 and 02 pods are Running.
close_reason: Verified 2026-09-28: obs-lab node Ready, all pods Running

title: Revert var.image to ubuntu-24.04 and delete snapshot 435320677
description:
var.image is pinned to snapshot 435320677 so the overnight destroy could be reversed with one apply. That pin is temporary and dangerous to leave: the moment the snapshot is deleted, an apply that used to work fails with a confusing 'image not found'.

Once the lab is back and confirmed healthy:
  1. Set var.image back to "ubuntu-24.04" in infra/variables.tf and restore the short description.
  2. Delete snapshot 435320677 via the snapshot workflow.

Note obs-snu covers the other snapshot, 435274711 (pre-rescale).
acceptance_criteria: infra/variables.tf has image defaulting to ubuntu-24.04, and snapshot 435320677 is gone from the snapshot list.
close_reason: var.image back to ubuntu-24.04 with image in ignore_changes (b104fbd, plan: no changes); snapshot 435320677 deleted

title: Pin the resolved Jenkins plugin set
description: installLatestPlugins stays at the chart default (latest dependency versions) because minimum resolution broke the Declarative Pipeline plugins (c80a586). So a reinstall can still get newer plugins than today. Export the working set (pluginManager/api/json, shortName:version) and list it in controller.installPlugins, then set installLatestPlugins: false and confirm zero inactive plugins and no SEVERE lines at startup.
